title: BESSELJ 56-row probe: three enumerated misses, all inherited from Excel COS
status_plain: BESSELJ was probed separately from BESSELY: a 56-row two-way probe over orders 0, 1, 2, 3, 5 and 10 with x in [1.5, 400]. The source says every row was bit-exact except three - BESSELJ(50,0) and BESSELJ(150,0) at 1 ULP and BESSELJ(50,2) at 2 ULP - and attributes all three away from Bessel: Excel's COS is 1 ULP off at the reduced arguments 49.214601836 and 149.214601836, probed directly, with SIN exact; J0 inherits cos at full weight. So a denominator (56) and a closed, enumerated miss set (3) both exist, and a 53-of-56 reading is derivable - but the source publishes NO fraction, and this record does not compose one. The three rows close automatically when SIN/COS parity lands; they are tracked with BUG-FUNC-027 CLASS-C3. Whether the 56 validation rows are disjoint from the 92 BESSELJ/I/K probe rows that fed the coefficient fit is not stated.

ruled_out: A BESSELJ defect as the cause of the three residual rows: Excel COS was probed directly at the reduced arguments and is 1 ULP off, with SIN exact.
open_question: The source does not say whether the 56 validation rows are disjoint from the 92-row BESSELJ/I/K probe set that fed the coefficient fit.
